situation_recap.text: Harborline is a Crestmark-sponsored, vertically integrated furniture designer and retailer (118 showrooms, FY2025 revenue **$1.42bn**). The collapse in existing home sales drove same-store sales down 9% in FY2024 and **14% in FY2025**, compounded by tariffs raising case-goods landed costs by ~18% and a failed ERP migration.

Adj. EBITDA fell from $212mm (FY2022) to $71mm (FY2025), margin compressing from 12.4% to **5.0%**; with **$1.35bn** of funded debt (ABL, $850mm 1st Lien TLB, $360mm 2nd Lien Notes), leverage reached **19.3x**. The Bank holds **$45.0mm** of the 1st Lien TLB.

After a failed turnaround, the Company engaged restructuring advisors in February 2026, skipped the March 2026 2nd Lien coupon and entered ABL forbearance; the credit was downgraded to **Doubtful in April 2026**.

recent_development.text: Harborline filed **Chapter 11 on August 4, 2026** (D. Del.) with an RSA supported by ~78% of the 1st Lien TLB, including the Bank. A **$150mm DIP** ($100mm new money, $50mm 1st Lien roll-up) received final approval; the Bank did not participate.

Under the Plan, 1st Lien lenders receive pro-rata a **$150mm Exit Term Loan** and **85% of reorganized equity** (subject to a 10% MIP); 2nd Lien receives 15% plus warrants; GUCs share a $6mm cash pool, with cramdown if the class rejects; sponsor equity is cancelled.

Provision increased from $18.0mm to **$29.3mm (65% of exposure)** in September 2026, an increase of **$12.3mm**, driven by the Disclosure Statement EV of **$420mm** vs. $600mm previously assumed, implying ~35% 1st Lien recovery.

checks.llm_issue: Memo states the increase was $11.3mm, not $12.3mm.

recent_development.text: The Bank's estimated recovery of **$15.7mm** comprises ~$7.9mm of Exit TL and ~4.5% of reorganized equity. The Disclosure Statement hearing is set for **October 28, 2026**, with emergence targeted for Q1 2027.
